title: RhodesMoore Post-Call Debrief, Research & Next-Steps Playbook
subtitle: Complete 28-Minute Call Breakdown, Technical Research Answers & Action Plan for Tobias Brousil

chapters.title: 1. Call Verdict & The Partner-Deal Gate
chapters.summary: Why the 28-minute walkthrough with John DeWald and Carolann Flaim-Neff was a clear win, how your Amazon Games engineering story landed, and why everything holds for their December or January partner close.

chapters.title: 2. Confirmed Portfolio & Wave 1-2-3 Sequence
chapters.summary: Yes, the properties are active! Breaking down Wave 1 Corporate Synergy, Wave 2 Hilo (Seniors Core) and Serosun Farms (Phase 1 Ops + Phase 2 Ramp), and Wave 3 Solana Beach and Mount Acadia.

chapters.title: 3. Four-Phase Lifecycle & Going Up the Tree
chapters.summary: Mapping John's four project stages (Concept, Political Entitlement, Construction plus 6-Month Pre-Leasing Reservation List, and Operational Portal) plus upward corporate validation.

chapters.title: 4. Research #1: SEO to AI Discovery (GEO)
chapters.summary: Answering John's question on impressing AI systems: why authoritative informational content beats sales fluff, llms.txt manifests, schema.org entity graphs, and demographic separation.

chapters.title: 5. Research #2: Escaping Web.com & Bus-Factor
chapters.summary: Comparing Cloudflare Pages, Vercel Pro, and AWS CloudFront alongside GoDaddy DNS, Microsoft 365 email safety, and eliminating John's past Ukraine-vendor lock-in risk via GitHub.

chapters.title: 6. Real iPhone Photos, Drones & Content Calendar
chapters.summary: Addressing John's dislike of stock photo packages, dispatching local FAA Part 107 drone pilots in Hawaii and Chicago, automated calendar nudges, and our 3 sample content pieces.

chapters.title: 7. Logos, Design Guide & Per-LLC Check Billing
chapters.summary: Standardizing fonts and styles across entities, rapid logo concepts plus game-industry illustrators, 50/50 piecemeal SOWs, and Carolann's per-LLC company check accounting.

chapters.title: 8. Your 4 Stakeholder Follow-Up & Request Emails
chapters.summary: Walking through the exact requests going to John, to Carolann on GoDaddy domains and Web.com plans, to their IT group on DNS, and your staged deal-close kickoff email.

chapters.title: 9. Driving Away Ready: Your Pre-Close Game Plan
chapters.summary: Everything we logged into your Master Work Plan today, optimal timing for your follow-up emails, and how to stay effortlessly top-of-mind until their partner deal signs.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Welcome back, Tobias! Put the car in drive, settle in, and take a victory lap, because we just went through every single second of your twenty-eight minute call with John DeWald and Carolann Flaim-Neff, and Alex, let's not bury the lead here. That call could not have gone smoother.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: It really was a textbook principal-to-principal conversation. And Tobias, the reason it worked so well is that you didn't sound like a thirsty agency salesperson trying to force a retainer today. You listened, you answered architectural questions cleanly on the fly, and right around the twenty-five minute mark, John literally paused after reading the final pricing table and said, 'All right, I think I understand it. It looks good.'

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: And let's talk about the big timing headline right up front so you have the whole chessboard in your head while you drive. Why aren't they signing a check this afternoon, and why is that actually totally fine?

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Because everything is gated on closing their pending joint venture partner transaction. John was super transparent about it. He said the exact closing date is still a little uncertain, hopefully very soon, targeting a December or January rollout. And Tobias, you asked the exact right closing question at minute twenty-five. You asked whether he wanted to start the RhodesMoore dot com refresh ahead of time, or hold that too.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: And John's answer actually made total architectural sense! He said yes, wait on RhodesMoore dot com too, because they want visual commonality, shared fonts, and real synergy across RhodesMoore, the new partner corporate sites, and the upcoming project sites.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Exactly. Plus, remember that at the time of the phone call, John hadn't even laid eyes on your live RhodesMoore concept study or the eight-minute 4K walkthrough yet! So you already won verbal buy-in on the architecture, the phased pricing, the fifty-fifty payment split, and per-LLC invoicing purely from your PDF and how you carried yourself on the phone. Now that you've sent him the thank-you link to shloobsoft dot net slash rhodesmoore, watching that 4K video is going to cement you as the obvious choice while they wrap up legal on their partner deal.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Oh, and one moment around minute fourteen made me smile. When John couldn't remember the name of old website builders like WordPress, you explained how fast AI tooling has shifted over the last six months, and mentioned building internal workflow tools at Amazon Games supporting six hundred and fifty engineers and non-technical artists. John immediately cracked that joke asking if you're the guy to blame for not being able to reach a human at Amazon, and both of you laughed. That completely broke the ice and established total technical authority.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Let's jump into Chapter Two, because right in the first sixty seconds of the recording, John solved the biggest mystery we had going into today. Remember before the call, we weren't sure if Hilo, Solana Beach, Serosun Farms, and The Pavilion on RhodesMoore dot com were just old historical examples or live upcoming builds.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Turns out they are very much real, active projects! And John laid out the exact three-wave sequence they plan to roll out as soon as the partner deal closes.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Let's walk through that sequence so it's locked in your memory. Wave One, targeting December or January right upon closing the deal, is all about Corporate Brochureware synergy. You'll rework RhodesMoore dot com alongside one or two of the new partner corporate or joint venture sites, establishing a standardized corporate design guide so all of them feel like part of the same institutional family.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Then comes Wave Two, starting right after the New Year. John specifically named two lead properties for Wave Two: Hilo on the Big Island of Hawaii, and Serosun Farms, which John pronounces Sair-uh-sen Farms, outside Chicago.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: And pay close attention to the distinct role of each of those two Wave Two sites, because we logged both into your Master Work Plan today. First, John said Hilo will be the base core template for their entire Seniors Community structure. That means when we engineer Hilo cleanly, its layout and lifecycle modules become the repeatable blueprint for every senior living community that follows.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Whereas Serosun Farms is the fascinating curveball. John explained that Serosun is more complicated for two reasons. First, Phase One is already partly built and operating while they ramp up Phase Two, so they want completed-community features on Serosun sooner rather than later. Second, while Serosun will include a seniors structure, it also services multiple other active business components on the property, like the working organic farm, equestrian facilities, event venue, and custom homesites.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: And then right behind Hilo and Serosun comes Wave Three: Solana Beach here in North County San Diego, Mount Acadia, which is their street-name shorthand for The Pavilion at Tecolote Canyon on Mount Acadia Boulevard in Clairemont, plus what John called a couple more related projects behind those. So we are genuinely looking at a multi-year, eight-to-twelve-plus site ecosystem across San Diego, Hawaii, and Chicago.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Which brings us to Chapter Three: how those project websites evolve over time, and how they connect back to corporate. On the call, John actually refined our three-stage model into four very specific real-world phases.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Let's trace all four phases John described between minutes one and twelve, because we updated both your Proposal Version Two and your internal platform roadmap to match his exact language. Phase One is Concept: advertising the initial project concept in a clean, fairly fixed manner.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Phase Two is Design and Entitlement, which John called 'a little more political.' At this stage, you aren't trying to lease apartments to seniors yet. You're communicating with the surrounding neighborhood and hosting materials for city managers, planning commissioners, and local politicians who are reviewing and approving the project.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Then Phase Three is Construction, and here is where you asked a brilliant question on the call, Tobias. At minute eleven, you asked John whether civic and political content stays side-by-side when a site moves into construction and pre-leasing, or whether it's a clean cutover. That prompted John to share a crucial operational detail: right in the middle of construction, roughly six months before construction finishes, they start building an Interest List, or Reservation List, for prospective senior residents and their adult children.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: So during that six-month pre-opening window, you have overlapping audiences! Neighbors and subcontractors still care about construction milestones, while families searching for senior care for a parent are joining the reservation list. John loved the idea of mapping out a phase-by-demographic overlap graphic, and your architectural answer at minute twenty-four nailed it: atop our shared core, a site can either make a clean cutover or use split visitor routing so civic visitors go one path and prospective families go another.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: And finally, Phase Four is Operational: once construction finishes, the site serves as an ongoing seniors and community portal communicating with residents, their families, and the surrounding neighborhood, with optional integration bridges into third-party operating and management software. Plus, across all four phases, John emphasized one non-negotiable rule he called 'going up the tree.'

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Meaning whenever a mayor, city planner, general contractor, architect, or vendor lands on a single project site like Hilo or Solana Beach, there must be a clear institutional pathway to click 'up the tree' to RhodesMoore and the partner corporate sites, proving that this isn't a one-off developer, it's a real firm backed by a deep portfolio.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Now let's dive into Chapter Four, which is the first of the two major technical research projects you promised John on the call: what is replacing traditional SEO in the age of AI, and whether RhodesMoore's authoritative informational content still matters.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Listen to how John phrased this at minutes nine and eighteen, because it tells you so much about how he thinks. First, he said his understanding is that traditional SEO may be going out, and what they really need to impress now are AI systems, tailored differently for early civic audiences versus later families looking for senior care. Then at minute eighteen, he said: 'There's always the BS sales copy stuff, we actually have some authoritative content that we can create or have created that used to be useful on SEO, I don't know if anybody cares about it anymore.'

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: And here is the headline of the research report we built for you today in RhodesMoore SEO AI Discovery and Hosting Report dot html: John's gut instinct against BS sales copy is one hundred percent validated by how modern AI search actually works! In the industry, this shift is called Generative Engine Optimization, or G-E-O.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Here's why. When an adult daughter types into ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, or Claude, 'What are the best single-story assisted living or memory care options in Hilo, Hawaii, and how does pricing work?', AI models don't count repeated keywords like a 2013 search engine. They actively strip out fluffy marketing adjectives like 'world-class luxury living,' and they hunt for concrete, verifiable facts and clear educational answers they can quote and cite.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: So in Part One of your new follow-up brief, we lay out a three-layer technical architecture that turns RhodesMoore's authoritative content into catnip for AI engines. Layer One is deploying a root llms dot txt file on every corporate and project domain. Just like robots dot txt guided old web crawlers, llms dot txt is a clean plain-text manifest at the root of each site that hands ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity an instant, hallucination-free fact sheet of the property, its exact phase, care levels, acreage, sustainability specs, and parent developers.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Layer Two is machine-readable Schema dot org JSON-LD entity graphs. On corporate sites, we publish Organization schema listing every sub-project. On project sites, we publish Place and SeniorCommunity schema with a parentOrganization pointer right back up the tree to RhodesMoore and the JV partners, plus FAQPage schema. That way, AI knowledge graphs verify that RhodesMoore is a two-hundred-million-dollar-plus developer with LEED Gold and Silver execution.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: And Layer Three is formatting their authoritative articles with front-loaded forty-to-sixty-word direct answer blocks, separated cleanly by project phase! During Phase Two Entitlement, the site publishes factual civic Q-and-As on traffic flow, coastal sightlines, solar generation, and stormwater stewardship, so if a neighbor or council member asks Google or ChatGPT about the project, the AI cites RhodesMoore's verified engineering facts instead of neighborhood rumor threads. Then six months before opening, we activate Google Business Profile, consistent local directory data, and family decision guides on Assisted Living versus Memory Care.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: We also included the current-site audit snapshot you promised at minute nineteen: pointing out gently that RhodesMoore's 2013 Web dot com site currently has zero JSON-LD schema, zero llms dot txt, non-responsive desktop layouts, and broken external links, while Serosun Farms has rich master-plan data locked inside an old 2013 PDF alongside those three compromised PHP directories that actively hurt search and AI trust until we migrate onto a clean read-only host.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Which leads directly into Chapter Five and Research Project Number Two: replacing Web dot com and picking the right cloud hosting stack alongside GoDaddy and their IT group.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: At minute seventeen, Carolann spoke up to confirm a key infrastructure fact: they finally consolidated ownership of all their domains onto GoDaddy, while their external IT group manages DNS and corporate email. And right after that, John vented about Web dot com. He said Web dot com might be fine for a tiny retail shop, but it is way too rigid to deviate from their template structure, and you can't get a knowledgeable human on the phone. He explicitly asked you to recommend, help sell internally, and port everything onto a flexible hosting platform.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: You promised him a number-one primary recommendation plus one or two backup options with clear pros and cons, so we built that exact comparison table into Part Two of your follow-up brief. Our Primary Recommendation is Cloudflare Pages plus Edge Workers.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Let's tick through why Cloudflare Pages is such a slam dunk for John, Carolann, and their IT group. First, cost and bandwidth: infrastructure runs zero to twenty dollars a month total, with completely unmetered bandwidth across more than three hundred global edge cities, including San Diego, Chicago, and Honolulu. That means high-resolution iPhone photo galleries and aerial drone loops load instantaneously without bandwidth overage bills.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Second, total architectural freedom with zero PHP or SQL attack surface. Every deployment is a read-only immutable build at the edge, making that Serosun Farms directory-injection hack mathematically impossible. And third, zero friction with GoDaddy and IT: domains stay registered in Carolann's GoDaddy account, Microsoft 365 email records stay one hundred percent untouched, and cutover only requires two standard web A or CNAME records per domain.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: And what about the two backup options in case their IT group asks?

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Backup Option One is Vercel Pro at twenty dollars a month. Pro: best-in-class instant staging preview links for reviewing edits before publishing, and super clean dynamic portal support. Con: bandwidth is metered above one terabyte per month if they ever stream heavy raw video directly. Backup Option Two is AWS CloudFront plus S3 on Amazon's fifteen-dollar-per-month Pro flat-rate bundle, which includes fifty terabytes of transfer on Amazon's global backbone. Pro: institutional AWS pedigree you know cold from Amazon. Con: AWS IAM permissions are heavier to administer if a non-AWS developer ever steps in later.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: And speaking of another developer ever stepping in, let's highlight minute twenty-three! When you mentioned that RhodesMoore owns one hundred percent of the Stage Two backbone upon payment, John immediately leaned in and asked: 'So we'd have the source or whatever it is, so if somebody else had to take over, they've got a starting point?' And then he revealed why: years ago, before the war, they used a software vendor with salespeople in Chicago and developers in Ukraine, and he doesn't even know if that company still exists!

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: That revelation was pure gold. So in both your follow-up brief and the updated Master Services Agreement, we explicitly guarantee that from Day One, all website source code, documentation, and their standardized Corporate Design Guide live inside a RhodesMoore-owned GitHub repository in clean, standard HTML, CSS, and TypeScript. Zero proprietary Web dot com lock-in, zero offshore black box, and a principal architect right up the road in San Marcos.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Now let's hit Chapter Six, which covers three practical capability questions where you wanted to make sure John feels zero hesitation: real site photography, multi-state drone video, and content generation.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: First, photography. At minute four, right after you mentioned cleaning up old cut-and-paste cars on legacy renderings, John shared a really important preference. Remember he hadn't seen your prototype yet, so he worried 'revamping pictures' might mean dropping in generic stock photography packages. He said they want to be honest with visitors so nobody drives out to a property and says, 'Well, I went there and that doesn't look like that.' Instead, they have lots of nice, real iPhone photos from their sites.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: And our follow-up turns that concern into a massive win! We explicitly commit to an Authentic Site Photography First rule, zero generic stock packages. We explain that they simply upload or text their raw on-site iPhone shots, and ShloobSoft runs them through an optical polish pipeline: straightening horizons, balancing harsh shadows and overcast skies, and encoding crisp 4K WebP galleries while keeping the actual property one hundred percent authentic. Even on your live prototype right now, Serosun's stone monument and Pacific Station's courtyard are their real photos, and The Pavilion includes a one-click toggle right back to the architect's exact 2022 drawings.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Second, at minute nineteen, John asked about drone video capture across San Diego, Hawaii, and Chicago. You handled the boundary honestly on the call, confirming that if they supply raw drone footage, you take it and run with all editing, color grading, and web streaming. Then in our research today, we went one step further to solve his Hawaii and Chicago logistics headache!

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: We researched the top three nationwide on-demand FAA Part 107 commercial drone networks: Zeitview, formerly DroneBase, FlyGuys, and Droners dot io. All three have vetted, insured local Part 107 pilots already on the ground on the Big Island of Hawaii, in Greater Chicago, and in San Diego, typically running three hundred to four hundred fifty dollars per flight with zero travel airfare. So whenever John wants fresh aerials over Hilo or Serosun Farms, ShloobSoft can write the exact architectural shot list, dispatch a local pilot, and edit the raw 4K footage into the site!

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Third, let's talk about content generation versus content management at minute eight. John was refreshingly candid: he said your clear superpower is technical architecture and building the sites, and what he hasn't experienced yet is your content writing capability, plus he wants a proactive Content Calendar that reminds them monthly or quarterly to send updates, while letting local community staff contribute social posts and photos.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: You offered on the call to put together some hypothetical samples so he can judge for himself with zero pressure, and we wrote three tailored, non-fluffy samples right into Part Three of your brief! Sample A is a calm, factual Phase Two Design and Entitlement neighbor update for Solana Beach covering sightlines, coastal canopy screening, and on-site turnaround traffic. Sample B is a Serosun Farms spring update weaving together certified organic cover crops, equestrian trail grading, and Phase Two one-acre conservation homesites. And Sample C is a Hilo senior living family guide excerpt explaining single-story plantation cottage living for kupuna on Hawaii Island, paired with a warm local Facebook post.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Paired with those three samples, we outline your Automated Content Calendar and Non-Technical Contributor workflow: automated monthly or quarterly email nudges where John or a local community manager can literally reply with two bullet points and three iPhone photos, or tap a guardrailed one-click form that makes it impossible to break fonts or page layouts.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Let's move into Chapter Seven: logos, the standardized design guide, and Carolann's multi-LLC check billing.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: At minute twenty, John looked at the Optional Logo and Brand Identity Kit in Section Three and asked whether you have graphic designers or use AI now. Your answer hit the exact right pragmatic note: starting from an idea, you generate five or six distinct visual concepts rapidly so they don't pay bloated agency fees upfront, and if they ever want custom human illustration polish, you have a deep Rolodex of veteran video-game studio artists you can tap immediately. John liked that and added that he wants to standardize fonts and visual conventions into a shared corporate design guide, which we folded directly into Stage Two.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Then at minutes twenty-six and twenty-seven came the business and accounting handshake! You proposed modular Statements of Work billed fifty percent upfront and fifty percent on delivery, piecemeal as each site or phase kicks off, with split invoices per LLC. John immediately agreed and explained why that matters so much internally: each development project sits inside its own separate set of LLCs distinct from the corporate entity, and Carolann's accounting team assigns expenses and cuts company checks from each specific LLC.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: We updated both Proposal Version Two and your Master Services Agreement template today to explicitly codify fifty-fifty milestone invoicing, piecemeal task orders, separate invoices addressed to each corporate or project LLC, and payment via company check or ACH on Net 15 terms. Carolann won't have to untangle a single mixed invoice.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Now, Chapter Eight: let's walk through the four ready-to-send stakeholder follow-up and request emails we built for you at localhost 8888 in RhodesMoore FollowUp Emails Suite dot html, so you know exactly what we're asking from each person at RhodesMoore.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Email One goes to John and Carolann together, attaching the two clean PDFs: your AI, Hosting, and Sample Content Brief, plus Updated Proposal Version Two. After recapping the Wave One through Three plan and the Cloudflare and AI search takeaways, it includes four polite, zero-rush optional requests for John ahead of closing: first, snapping a photo if he sketches that phase-by-demographic overlap diagram he mentioned; second, sending one or two examples of RhodesMoore's existing authoritative articles so you can run a concrete AI-search formatting audit on them; third, optionally sharing two or three raw on-site iPhone photos from Hilo or Serosun if he wants to see a real before-and-after polish sample; and fourth, his thoughts once he watches the 4K walkthrough and reads the three content samples.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Email Two is a short, thoughtful administrative note addressed directly to Carolann, copying John. Again, framed as zero rush ahead of December or January, it asks Carolann for three helpful prep items: first, a quick list or screenshot of the domains currently consolidated inside GoDaddy, plus which domains still have active Web dot com subscriptions so you can help cancel Web dot com cleanly after migration without double-billing; second, an introduction to their IT group contact whenever ready; and third, offering your signed W-9 now so she can set ShloobSoft up as a vendor across their separate LLC checkbooks ahead of Wave One.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Email Three is ready for their IT Group contact as soon as Carolann or John makes that introduction, or Carolann can simply forward it. It reassures IT in the very first paragraph that GoDaddy registrar ownership and Microsoft 365 email records stay one hundred percent untouched in their hands, explains the two-record Cloudflare edge cutover, and asks IT two simple technical questions: whether they prefer applying two DNS records from a cutover sheet or using scoped GoDaddy delegate access, and whether any legacy subdomains besides rhodesmoore dot invportal dot com need to be preserved when Web dot com is retired.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: And Email Four stays tucked in your pocket for the day John emails in December or January saying the partner deal close is imminent. With one click, it congratulates them and requests the five exact Wave One kickoff inputs: the partner corporate names and domains, Carolann's final LLC split list for the fifty percent deposit invoices, any existing logos, raw copy bullets, and a shared folder for Hilo and Serosun iPhone photos.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Finally, let's wrap up in Chapter Nine with your game plan from today until deal close. Everything John and Carolann shared today has been logged into your Master Work Plan artifact, including upgrading our internal white-label community engine from three stages to John's exact four phases, adding the persistent 'Go Up the Tree' corporate validation bar, baking in automatic llms dot txt and JSON-LD generators, and prepping the Content Calendar email-nudge workflow.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: As for timing your emails: you already have the quick thank-you email with the shloobsoft dot net slash rhodesmoore link out first so John and Carolann can enjoy the interactive refresh concept and the 4K walkthrough without an inbox full of attachments. Give that a little breathing room, say late this afternoon or tomorrow morning, then send Email One with the two exported PDFs, followed a day or two later, or right alongside it, by Email Two to Carolann.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: After that, you don't have to chase or pester them while they close a complex real estate partnership. You've given them a live 4K prototype, an Amazon-caliber technical brief on AI discovery and cloud hosting, three custom writing samples, and a clean per-LLC execution plan. Whenever that partner deal inks in December or January, you're already standing at the starting line ready to roll.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Seriously awesome work on that call today, Tobias. Enjoy the rest of your drive, and whenever you're back at your desk, everything is organized and waiting on your local Command Center!
